    Graded Ext from graded projective resolutions (Lemma 6.3) #

    positive-deformations.tex: "Internal degree t in Hom or Ext means maps from a graded projective resolution to the target which raise degree by t." This file defines that Ext and compares it with the bar Ext (ExtVanish) used in the rest of the formalization.

    • GProj: a graded projective module (degree-zero graded module maps lift along graded surjections). Finitely generated ones are retracts of finite sums of shifted regular modules (exists_free_cover), so their bar Ext vanishes (GProj.extVanish).
    • GRes: a graded projective resolution ⋯ → P₁ → P₀ → M → 0 (finitely generated graded projectives, maps of degree 0, exact). GRes.ExtVanish: Ext^{n+1}(M, N)_t = 0 computed from it, i.e. every degree-t graded module map P_{n+1} → N vanishing on the image of P_{n+2} factors through P_{n+1} → P_n by a degree-t graded module map.
    • GRes.extVanish_iff: for every graded projective resolution, this vanishing is the bar vanishing. In particular it does not depend on the resolution. Over a commutative ring R (a field, or ℤ/4 in Lemma 6.6) it assumes the graded pieces of Λ and M projective over R (for the free modules of Lemma 6.6, and automatically over a field: GRes.extVanish_iff_field).
    • exists_gres: a finitely generated graded module over a module-finite graded algebra over a noetherian ring has a graded projective resolution.

    So every Ext vanishing hypothesis or conclusion stated in the bar form (Lemma 6.3, Propositions 6.5, 10.1, Lemma 6.6) is equivalent to the manuscript's form for any graded projective resolution.
